hearingHeaders.I: G1 Schedule: county, in writing (per docket)
hearingHeaders.J: G2 Consultant's own yes for this slot
hearingHeaders.K: G3 County has the name on record for this case
hearingHeaders.L: G4 Evidence on file with the clerk
hearingHeaders.O: G5 Proof that it is processed
hearingHeaders.P: Grade of weakest proof so far
hearingHeaders.Q: Day-before YES (video or phone: with the link or number)
hearingHeaders.T: Error at the hearing (from the same-day result)
hearingHeaders.AB: Example note: what the two AI readers found
hearingHeaders.AC: Yes by the offer's deadline? (yes / no)
hearingHeaders.AL: Row of the hearing before it in the docket (formula)
hearingHeaders.AN: Offer list so far, open hearings only (formula)
hearingHeaders.AQ: Docket sequence, on the last row of each docket (formula)
hearingHeaders.AR: In sorted order? 1 = yes, 0 = no, -1 = this row no longer reads its own row: the row or one of its typed cells was cut and pasted or dragged (also to another tab), cells were inserted or deleted, or a row was inserted above it (formula)
hearingHeaders.AS: Hearings this consultant holds in the docket (formula)
hearingHeaders.AT: Day-before texts so far, one for each consultant (formula)
hearingHeaders.AU: Status still holds its formula? 1 = yes (formula)
hearingHeaders.AV: Room, video link or call-in number (from the office; an arrival instruction goes in column CI, as minutes)
hearingHeaders.AW: Office's deadline for this row (date and time, from its message)
hearingHeaders.AY: Case files: version the consultant confirmed (GOT IT)
hearingHeaders.AZ: Case files: version the clerk confirmed (every file named)
hearingHeaders.BA: Owed by (date and time, as the office wrote it)
hearingHeaders.BB: Owed: last working moment to send it (formula)
hearingHeaders.BD: Name on the office's record (as its message says)
hearingHeaders.BF: Notice list so far: yes replies whose name the office does not have yet (formula)
hearingHeaders.BG: Homeowner's written yes for a settlement or withdrawal (link)
hearingHeaders.BH: Times the office has asked about this row (count each reminder)
hearingHeaders.BI: Our date-change request: the date we asked
hearingHeaders.BJ: The office's written answer to our date-change request (link)
hearingHeaders.BK: Name on the homeowner's notice (as the firm sent it)
hearingHeaders.BL: Date on the homeowner's notice (as the firm sent it)
hearingHeaders.BM: Case files: send by, 48 hours before the hearing (formula)
hearingHeaders.BN: To tell the consultant: a change from the office or a wrong belief (who, what, which message)
hearingHeaders.BO: Told, or they already have it: link to their own message or their OK
hearingHeaders.BR: Consultant said they are not free then (formula)
hearingHeaders.BW: GOT IT is from (type the consultant's name with the link in M)
hearingHeaders.BX: Day-before YES is from (type the name with the link in Q)
hearingHeaders.BY: Offer out to (type the name when the offer goes; clear it at their no)
hearingHeaders.BZ: Held by, or on offer to (formula)
hearingHeaders.CA: Over the daily cap: 1 on the first row of that consultant's day, 0 on its other rows (formula)
hearingHeaders.CB: Time-zone sentence for the texts to consultants (formula)
hearingHeaders.CC: Office's deadline in force: column AW, or else the office's standing naming rule from Offices AF (formula)
hearingHeaders.CE: Next-step lines for column BE: the office's own route, the homeowner's notice, a missed hearing, proofs missing after the hearing (formula)
hearingHeaders.CF: Travel gap at this office around an in-person hearing, minutes (formula)
hearingHeaders.CG: Travel gap at this office between video sessions, minutes (formula)
hearingHeaders.CH: Arrival time the consultant gave (if they gave one)
hearingHeaders.CI: Office's own arrival instruction for this hearing: minutes before the first case (number, if the office gave one; type it on every hearing of the docket)
hearingHeaders.CJ: Link check for a video or telephone hearing: 0 not one, 1 a link or number is in AV, 2 the room letter is all the office sends, 3 the room is at the office, 4 a room or words only and the office has not said, 5 AV is empty (formula)
hearingHeaders.CK: Counts as in person for the travel check and the arrival text: 1 = yes (formula)
hearingHeaders.CL: Time the firm needs the consultant at the office, in minutes after midnight (formula)
hearingHeaders.CM: More lines for column BE: a video room without a link, a receipt that names no version, a first case at opening, a later arrival time (formula)
hearingHeaders.CN: Length of one hearing at this office, minutes: Offices AP, or else Settings B11 (formula)
hearingHeaders.CO: Starts at opening: 1 when a coming hearing starts less than Settings B17 minutes after its office opens (formula)
hearingHeaders.CP: The office says it cannot find our notice (link to its message or to the dated call note)
hearingHeaders.CQ: Our notice or form for this hearing went to the office on (date, or the link to the sent message)
hearingHeaders.CR: Homeowner agreed to the new date we asked the office for (link; belongs with BI and BJ)
hearingHeaders.CS: Bench asked first, before the office was asked to move the hearing (link to the dated note of who was asked and said no; belongs with BI and BJ)
hearingHeaders.CT: Still attending after an illness report (link to the consultant's own yes)
hearingHeaders.CU: Date of that yes (it counts from the day of the illness report on)
hearingHeaders.CV: Office's hours from UTC on the hearing date: Offices W, plus one hour in United States daylight time when Offices AU says yes (formula)
hearingHeaders.CW: How the consultant on the row can be reached: 2 = text and call, 1 = call only, 0 = email only, from Bench R (formula)
hearingHeaders.CX: Office route state, from Offices AV: 0 no change, 1 a change waits for approval (blocked), 2 the new route only, 3 the new route and the old one (formula)
hearingHeaders.CY: Illness: the day this consultant reported ill, when this hearing falls in the days after it and no later yes is linked (formula)
hearingHeaders.CZ: Round 16 lines for column BE: a notice the office cannot find, a call the route needs, a date-change request without the homeowner's yes, a settlement, an owed document, illness, no number, arrival not recorded (formula)
hearingHeaders.DA: Clearer copy asked on (the date of our request, or the link to it when the date is not known; clear the cell when a readable copy has come)
hearingHeaders.DB: Arrangement for a first case at opening made (link to the office's message or to the dated note: the end-of-docket request and the alternate)
hearingHeaders.DC: Settlement offer on file (link). A row is read as a settlement when column N holds the letters "settle", or when this cell holds a link or the next one a date
hearingHeaders.DD: The offer must be accepted by (date)
hearingHeaders.DF: Homeowner's customer number (from the case record; hearings of one homeowner carry the same number)
hearingHeaders.DG: Homeowner's contact (telephone or email, from the client file)
hearingHeaders.DH: A consultant had already accepted this hearing when we asked the office to move it (their name and the link to their yes; empty if nobody had)
hearingHeaders.DI: The office's answer to our date-change request (choose: moved / refused; belongs with BJ)
hearingHeaders.DJ: Row of this hearing's office on the Offices tab, or 9999999 when the county is not on it (formula)
hearingHeaders.DK: Arrival clash: the row of the Availability tab on which the consultant said they are not free at the arrival time in CL; 0 = none (formula)
hearingHeaders.DL: Arrival time the day-before text prints, minutes after midnight: CL; or CH when there is an arrival clash and CH holds a time; -1 while the clash is not settled (formula)
hearingHeaders.DM: Clearer copy: the moment the fallback falls due, noon on the working day Settings B14 after the date in DA (formula)
hearingHeaders.DN: The office's last day for a change request: the hearing date less the working days in Offices AY, by the office's holidays; empty while AY holds no number (formula)
hearingHeaders.DO: A line on this row orders a call to the homeowner: 1 = yes (formula)
hearingHeaders.DP: Round 17 lines for column BE: arrival not settled, the wait for a clearer copy, a moved hearing without the homeowner's yes, a request for a hearing already accepted, the office's last day for a change request, the homeowner to call, the office's number; and from round 18 a hearing that was moved while the homeowner has not got the new date (formula)
hearingHeaders.DQ: The office's record in column K is for the hearing date of (type the hearing date the office's message was about, with the link in K; on a hearing that was moved, K counts only while this is the date in column D)
hearingHeaders.DR: This hearing was moved: the date it had before (type it when an office moves a hearing, whoever asked for the move)
hearingHeaders.DS: The homeowner has the new date (link to their own message, to the dated call note or to the corrected notice sent)
hearingHeaders.DU: Link to the note or message that reported the result
hearingHeaders.DV: Date-change request decided by (name and date)
hearingHeaders.DW: Notice arrived on (date: the day the office's notice linked in column I reached the firm; type it for a paper notice and wherever a deadline counts from the arrival)
hearingHeaders.DX: The message behind the next action in column Y arrived on (date; type it when the message says today, tomorrow or this week, and type the real date in AA)
hearingHeaders.DY: The office's record in K counts for the date in column D: 1 = yes (formula)
hearingHeaders.DZ: Where a hearing in person is held: the office's street address, room and where to report from Offices BA, or ADDRESS NOT ON RECORD and the cell; empty for a hearing nobody attends in person (formula)
hearingHeaders.EA: Round 18 lines for column BE: the office's record after a move, a result with no source or not clear, who decided a date-change request, the office's address, a date in words, a paper notice with no arrival day (formula)
hearingHeaders.EB: Who asked for the date change (type: the firm, the homeowner, or the consultant and their name, with the message number; belongs with DR and DI)
hearingHeaders.EC: Files access removed from the earlier consultant (date, or 'files were never sent')
hearingHeaders.ED: Round 19 lines for column BE: who asked for a date change, whether the consultant may appear and sign in the office's state, case-file access of a consultant who left (formula)
hearingHeaders.EE: Keep this column empty: Dockets A1 reads it to notice cells pushed out of their columns

cells.A: The control sheet: one row per hearing, one link per proof

All rows are fictional examples from the case packet, and the example links do not open. The example shows the sheet after the 9:00 a.m. pass: the proof cells hold 60 links that the prototype's two AI readers proposed from the 72 example messages, and 20 more that a person added in that pass (17 of them are listed on the tab "Reader suggestions": the 16 of its second list of the 9:00 a.m. pass and 1 more that only its first list holds; the other 3 are consultants' own messages in column BO that show they already have a change) (the tab lists all 63 proposals to close a cell, 10 of them for the case files on words that name no version, shown there as "names no version: a person asks for it"; one message can prove several cells, and one cell needs only one link). In 2 of the readers' cells (the clerk's receipt for AX-121 and AX-122) the person pasted a later message from the same office over the readers' link, because it names the files as current. Delete the example rows as whole rows (select the row numbers, right-click, Delete) and start with your own hearings in the rows below, which already hold the formulas. The live copy is one shared online workbook for all counties, filtered by county, up to about 1,000 hearings a year; above that, one per county team. It is archived at the end of the season.

START HERE: what this sheet is and how to use it on a normal day
What this is: the gate sheet for the hearings of the season, one row per hearing on the Hearings tab. A hearing is ready only when each proof cell holds a link to the message that proves it. The rows in this copy are fictional examples.
The five tabs a coordinator uses every day: Hearings (one row per hearing; Status in W and the daily list in X), Reader suggestions (the 9:00 a.m. pass), Dockets (the offers and the day-before texts), Who can take it (whom to ask next), and Calendar (after the 2:00 p.m. review). Their tabs are blue.
The five columns typed on a normal day, all on the Hearings tab: H the consultant, J the consultant's own yes for the slot (a link), K the office's record of our name for the case (a link), BD the name on the office's record, and P the grade of the weakest proof.
Colours: blue cells are proof cells and take a link; pale blue cells take what a person types; grey cells are formulas and are never typed in. Amber cells hold a question still to ask and start with ASK. A red cell says, in words, what is due or wrong today; a green status is ready or done. Columns marked with a + above the headings hold helper formulas and are grouped out of the way.
Tabs: blue daily work, green records, orange setup (offices, bench, availability, holidays, settings), grey reference.
Help: the paragraphs below on this tab, in order, and the heading of each column, which says what goes in it.

The sheet runs in all ten counties from live week 2, with five checks for every hearing (Settings B6 = full). Every row starts from the county's notice, or a dated portal screenshot. G1 the county's schedule in writing; for a video or telephone hearing G1 also needs the link or the number in column AV. A room letter alone ("room C") is not a link: it counts only once the office has said that the room letter is all it sends (Offices AL). G2 the consultant's own yes for this slot; it stops counting the moment the Availability tab says they are not free then (column BV). G3 our consultant's name on the county's record, in writing, for this case: column BD names the person the office has, and if it is someone else G3 does not count. G4 the case files: the clerk's receipt naming every file, and the consultant's GOT IT, both for the current version in column AX; the GOT IT counts only for the consultant named beside it in column BW. A receipt that names no version does not close G4 while column AX holds the current version: type the version the message names in AZ (the clerk) or AY (the consultant); where it names none, column BE prints the question to send. G5 proof that anything owed was processed, and for a settlement or a withdrawal the homeowner's written yes in column BG first. The reply rule (node cli/replies.js, connected to the text line and the shared mailbox) files the consultant's fixed-form replies; the two AI readers propose the office's links on the "Reader suggestions" tab and a person accepts them in one pass at 9:00 a.m. About 4 minutes a hearing by hand, less with the rule and the readers (estimate).

Status says how far a hearing has got. Before the hearing: OPEN (n proofs missing), READY (every proof in), CONFIRMED (READY and the day-before YES of the consultant on the row, named in column BX), then the ARRIVED or IN time on the day. After it: RESULT DUE (no result yet), MISSED (nobody appeared; the row stays on the daily list until the good-cause letter is linked in column N and the office's answer in column O), OWED (a signature, statement or withdrawal is outstanding), NEW DATE DUE (postponed, the county's new date not in yet), ERROR DUE (the error entry is empty), DECISION DUE (heard, the board's written decision not linked in BQ), "RESULT IN: ARRIVAL NOT RECORDED" (the result is typed but column R holds no arrival or join time; the row stays on the daily list as ARRIVAL DUE until the time is typed), "DONE: n proofs missing" (held, but a proof never came in; it stays on the daily list as PROOFS DUE until every proof is linked) and DONE. The day-before YES is not asked for again once the hearing is over: DONE does not wait for it, and the Measures tab counts the hearings held without one. Also NOT HELD (cancelled, with the office's written proof), CANCEL PROOF DUE and NO DATE. That is how the firm knows the work is complete: a hearing is complete only at DONE.

A hearing is ready when each fact is confirmed by the party that owns the fact, and the cell links to the message that proves it. Nobody types "confirmed" or "ready": Status is a formula, and a cell counts only if it holds a link.

Per hearing: G2 the consultant's own yes for this slot, G3 the office's record for this case (an office may record one case of a docket and not the other: Orimere, message 16), and G4 the evidence on file with the clerk and with the consultant.

Per docket, once for all of an office's hearings that day: G1 the schedule. One reply or one dated portal screenshot is pasted into each of those rows. An office that says it "can record" someone, a voicemail, or a form sent that the office cannot find, is not a record: G3 stays empty until the office confirms in writing.
G5 needs a link only when something is owed (a signature, a withdrawal, a statement). If the county moves a hearing, clear G2: a yes belongs to a time slot.

A hearing by written statement (Format = written statement) has nobody in the room: G2 and the consultant's GOT IT do not apply, there is no offer, no day-before text, no CONFIRM TODAY and no arrival, a "not free" row does not open it, "Ask next" ranks nobody for it, it is not on the Calendar, not a consultant-day, not in a consultant's count of hearings that day, and not counted on the Measures tab in row 3 (hearings inside 3 working days with no yes) or row 15 (hearings per consultant-day), and it is READY when the office's notice, the name on its record and the clerk's receipt of the statement and files are linked. The office's deadline for the statement goes in AW.

The sheet needs Excel 2019 or later, Microsoft 365, or Google Sheets: it uses MINIFS and ISFORMULA, which older Excel lacks. This sheet (159,013 formulas) is recalculated and checked in LibreOffice 24.2. Two other programs were run on 20 and 21 Nov 2026 (measured). Excel for Mac, version 16: the 1,200-row sheet as it stood on 20 Nov, before a wording fix, the Google Sheets fix and the rules added on 21 Nov (143,729 formulas then) was opened, fully recalculated and saved: every formula was kept, no cell held an error value, and of 16,534 filled cells only the 42 of the random draw behind the Friday sample differed from LibreOffice. Google Sheets: an 80-row copy of this sheet as it stood before the rules added on 21 Nov (39,652 formulas then, the same formulas on every row) was converted and recalculated: every formula was kept, no cell held an error value, and the results matched LibreOffice except the random draw (45 cells) and 780 empty holiday cells that Google keeps blank where LibreOffice holds a hidden 0. That run first found two faults that only Google Sheets showed (unused rows of the Calendar tab were filled, and Dockets A1 reported an error value); both are fixed in this sheet, which is why column S of the Calendar file tab and the heading "Keep this column empty" of the Hearings tab exist (that heading was in DA1 then and is in EE1 now, one column to the right of the last column). The columns and lines added on 21 Nov (Hearings DA to ED, Offices AY to BB, Bench S and T, a helper column of the "Who can take it" tab, and the question formulas on rows 12 to 40 of the Offices tab) were run in LibreOffice only: an 80-row copy of the sheet as it is now has 41,413 formulas and recalculates there with no error value. Not tested: the full 1,200 rows in Google Sheets, Excel for Windows or in a browser, and typing, cutting, pasting, inserting, deleting or sorting rows in either program (those are LibreOffice results). So before the first live week, open this sheet in the program the firm will use, check that no cell shows an error value and that cell A1 of the Dockets tab reads "Rows are sorted: yes", and type one trial row.

A cancellation or withdrawal needs proof too. First link the homeowner's written yes in column BG (a person calls the homeowner if it is not in writing). Then set "Hearing still on?" to no. The hearing stays staffed and on its docket, with every check, until the office's written confirmation is linked in column AF; until then Status reads CANCEL PROOF DUE and the row stays on the daily list. An internal "cancelled" never takes a consultant off a hearing (Iverfen, messages 51 to 53). When the office's confirmation is linked, type the release notice for the consultant in column BN (who, and that the hearing is off): column BE prints TELL, and the Daily list reads TELL DUE, until their OK is linked in column BO.
What may go into a proof cell (the blue columns)

Only a link. A phone call, a portal page or a text has no link of its own: put them on one dated PDF per docket in the shared folder and link that. Consultants confirm by text or by reply to the shared mailbox; either way the yes has a link. Test all five kinds of proof on day 1. The limit: a proof cell takes any text that starts with http. The sheet cannot open a link or read what it says, so a link cell (for example column BO, the consultant's OK, and column DB, the arrangement for a first case at opening) counts whatever link is pasted there. The Friday sample is the check that a link says what its cell claims.

Grade of the weakest proof: A = the office's own written reply or notice, or the person's own message. B = a dated screenshot of the office's portal or docket. A phone call never closes a check: it goes in Next action with the name, time and what was said, the check stays open, and the office is asked to put it in writing.
Every day at 9:00 a.m. and at 2:00 p.m.

9:00 a.m.: one person accepts or rejects the readers' proposals on the "Reader suggestions" tab and reads the messages the readers handed to a person. The foot of that tab lists the proposals for the Offices tab (HOLD: an office changed how it works); each waits for the same person's yes or no. HOLD means: NO NOTICE GOES TO THIS OFFICE UNTIL A PERSON APPROVES THE CHANGE TODAY. While column M of the Offices tab holds a change and nobody has typed their name and the date in columns AQ and AR of that office, every line the sheet writes for that office prints the block and no route, and its hearings go to the TOP OF LIST. After the approval the new route is the route; the old route is printed as a second route only while column AS says yes or not known. 2:00 p.m.: filter the "Daily list" column for anything not empty. TOP OF LIST: a hearing within 3 working days with a proof missing, an office that has asked twice or more, or something owed within a working day. It gets a name and a due time before the review ends. REVIEW: a proof missing within 14 days. CONFIRM TODAY: the hearing is on the next working day and there is no day-before YES. RESULT DUE, ERROR DUE, NEW DATE DUE, DECISION DUE, OWED: see Status above. NOBODY NAMED: POSSIBLY MISSED: the hearing is over and no consultant was named; call the office today. DATE DUE: the row has no hearing date. CANCEL PROOF DUE: the hearing is marked as not on and column AF has no link. TELL DUE: the row has something to tell the consultant (column BN) with no OK linked yet (column BO), and nothing else has put the row on the list; this also holds after the hearing and at NOT HELD. TOP OF LIST: MISSED, LETTER DUE: nobody appeared and the good-cause letter is not linked in column N. MISSED: ANSWER DUE: the letter went and the office's answer is not linked in column O. PROOFS DUE: the hearing was held and a proof is still missing. Where an office has a standing naming deadline (Offices AF), its hearings go to the TOP OF LIST the working days of Settings B4 before that deadline, for as long as the office has not confirmed the name in writing.
Nothing is stamped by hand. "Ready on time" on the Measures tab counts itself from the formulas, and the Friday checker copies it into the weekly log.
Dockets: one offer and one day-before text for each office, day and format

Keep the Hearings tab sorted by date, then office, then time (select the rows, then Data, Sort). The Dockets tab builds itself from the rows: one line for each docket from today on, with the offer text, the day-before text, who holds hearings now, which numbers are open, the notice to the office and who to ask next. The offer lists only the open hearings, and the day-before text is written once for each consultant on the docket, with that consultant's own first time and number of hearings. A video or telephone docket with a link missing reads DO NOT SEND YET until column AV holds the link or the number, or the office has said that its room letter is all it sends (Offices AL). An in-person day-before text gives the time the firm needs the consultant at the office as a clock time: their first case less the minutes in Settings B16, or less the office's own instruction (column CI) when that asks for more. It names one time only. Both texts say once that the times are the office's local time, with its hours from UTC where the Offices tab has them (column W), for example "Times are Larkmere office time (UTC-05:00)." Cell A1 of the Dockets tab reads "Rows are sorted: yes", or it says in red what to put right.

Type a time as a time (9:30 or 1:30 pm). A time typed as text, such as 3:30 p.m. with the dots, is still read, but a sort puts it after the other times of its docket: cell A1 of the Dockets tab then names the row, and the time is typed again as a time. Add a hearing by copying a whole row, so its formulas come with it; never clear a row with the Delete key. Never cut and paste or drag a row or a single cell to another place, never insert a row between two hearings, and never use Insert cells or Delete cells: the formulas follow the cell that was moved, so a row can go on counting a link that is no longer in it, and a docket can drop off the Dockets tab. To move what a cell holds, copy it, paste it into the right cell, then empty the old cell with the Delete key. To move a hearing, sort the tab; to add one, use the first free row below the last hearing and sort. To take a hearing off, delete its whole row (right-click the row number, Delete rows). Type nothing to the right of column ED. Cell A1 of the Dockets tab names a row or a typed cell that was moved this way, a row whose cells were shifted to the side, and a row that lost a formula of column W, AR or ED. A typed cell that was cut and pasted to another tab is named whenever the cell that the formulas now read holds something else than the cell in its old place: at once if the cell held something, and for an empty cell as soon as something is typed in either place. Until then nothing is misread. The limit: a formula cell that is cut and pasted is seen only in columns W, AR and ED. A date typed as text (for example "to be set") makes its row read NO DATE, and cell A1 names the row. If a hearing is added to a docket or marked as not on after its offer went out, the numbers in that docket change: send the docket's offer again.

A hearing that a consultant has accepted stays with that consultant. The column "Offer this docket to" says whether to offer the docket whole to one consultant, or to offer the open numbers first to the consultant who is already on it or already at that office that day. "Ask next" ranks everyone else: at this office that day, said they are free then, primary or promised this weekday, preference fits, bench, then working elsewhere with the travel gap met; it leaves out anyone who declined, said they are not free, is full or cannot travel in time (codes on the "Who can take it" tab). The words for the fee and the telephone number come from Settings B7 and B8. No offer names a price. When an offer goes out, type the consultant's name in column BY of each hearing offered ("Offer out to"), and clear it at their no; their yes in G2 ends the offer by itself. Until then those hearings count in that consultant's day together with the hearings they hold, on every docket of that date, so nobody is offered more hearings on one date than "Most hearings a day" on the Bench tab, or two hearings too close in time. If a consultant still holds more than that, column BE prints OVER THE DAILY CAP on each of their rows that day and the Measures tab counts it.

"Tell the office" is the notice to send the day a yes arrives: who attends each case, from yes replies only, only for the cases the office does not yet have, in the office's own form (Offices AB), with our contact (Settings B10), our alternate once the office has accepted one, the replacement route, and the office's own deadline. When an office has told us of a change in how it works (Offices M), the notice is blocked until a person approves the change (Offices AQ and AR), and then names the new route. Before any notice already in a case folder goes out, check it on the "Notices on file" tab: only SEND IT goes; VOID is marked void in the folder and never sent.
The day before, and the day of

Day before: the text goes out at 8:00 a.m. on the working day before, names the date (never "tomorrow"), gives times in the office's local time and says so. The consultant's YES goes into "Day-before YES" (column Q) as a link, with their name in column BX; a YES counts only for the consultant named there. For a video or telephone hearing the text carries the link or the number from column AV. No YES by noon: phone. Still no YES at 2:00 p.m., or a NO: type one row on the Availability tab for that consultant, that date, marked not free, with the note "no day-before YES by 2 p.m." (a silent consultant is treated as out). The hearing turns open and red, the Dockets offer lists it and asks for an answer within one hour, and "Ask next" leaves the silent consultant out. Offer it to the first name in "Ask next". If the silent consultant answers YES before anyone else has, delete that row, put their name back in H with their YES in J, take it out of BC, and paste back anything of theirs that was cleared (their GOT IT in M with AY and BW, and their arrival time in CH). Still nobody at 4:00 p.m.: the office's alternate on record takes the docket and gets the files tonight; where the office has no alternate on record yet (Offices T), phone the next names in "Ask next" until one says yes. A dropout after 4:00 p.m. or overnight: the person named in Settings B9 texts everyone in "Ask next" at once (the first YES wins, the rule hands later ones to a person), emails the office and its alternate, and phones the office when it opens. Every dropout, at any hour, is one row on the Availability tab marked not free: the hearing turns open and red at once. Whoever takes it, the office is told the same day by its replacement route ("Tell the office"). On the row, clear the proofs of the consultant who left: H and J (the name and their yes), M, AY and BW (their GOT IT, its version and their name), Q and BX (their day-before YES and their name) and CH (the arrival time they gave). Then type the new name in H, paste the new consultant's own yes in J, send them the case files, and paste their GOT IT in M with the version in AY and their name in BW. BD changes when the office confirms the new name in writing. A replacement never inherits a GOT IT or a day-before YES: each counts only for the consultant named beside it, and until the cells are cleared column BE says whose proof it is. An arrival time is not inherited either: while BW or BX still names the consultant who left, column BE prints the time in CH as possibly theirs and not as the new consultant's.

Every Wednesday: one text or email to each consultant lists next week's dockets (filter the Consultant column). No YES ALL by Thursday noon: phone. A docket handed back on Thursday can still be offered to someone else.

In person: one named coordinator is on the phone from 45 minutes before the first hearing at each office. The consultant texts ARRIVED by the time in their day-before text: the first case less the minutes in Settings B16 (30). No ARRIVED by then: call. 15 minutes before: call the office and ask for our cases to go to the end of the docket. A consultant who names a later arrival time gets a reply the same day: type the time they gave in column CH, and column BE prints it against the time the firm needs; when they agree, type the agreed time over it. The time belongs to the consultant who gave it: clear CH when another consultant takes the hearing. An office's own arrival instruction goes in column CI as minutes, on every hearing of the docket; the text uses whichever asks for more. Where the first case starts less than 30 minutes after the office opens (Settings B17, Offices AM), nobody can reach the office before the hearing: column BE prints FIRST CASE AT OPENING from two working days before, and the end-of-docket request and the alternate are arranged on a working day before, while the office is open.

Video or telephone: the consultant texts IN ten minutes before. No IN five minutes before: the named alternate (the firm's attorney or registered agent, once on the county's record) joins from the office; until an office has accepted an alternate, the coordinator calls the office and asks for our cases to go to the end of the docket.

The consultant reports per hearing the same day: REDUCED to $___ / NO CHANGE / POSTPONED to ___ / NOT HEARD / DECISION TO FOLLOW, plus any problem with the file, the name, the date or the time. The coordinator enters the result and "Error at the hearing" ("none" if none), from the board's order where there is one; when the board sends its decision later, its link goes in column BQ. "nobody appeared" turns the row to MISSED, and the good-cause letter goes out that day: column BE prints the next step with the office's own way back (Offices P). Paste the link to the letter in column N after the words "good-cause letter", type the office's time limit in BA, and link the office's answer in O. The work on a missed hearing is complete when both are linked; a new hearing that the office grants is a new row.

Column BE prints, in red, everything due or changed on the row, and is read with the daily list: the office's deadline (AW, or else its standing naming rule in Offices AF, printed as the office's standing rule); OWED: SEND BY, moved to the office's last working day (BB); the homeowner's written yes missing; an office that has asked twice or more (BH); a decision still to come; a video link or number still missing; a name without a yes; a consultant who said they are not free; SEND CASE FILES VERSION n, 48 hours before (BM), or past that mark with a request to the clerk to accept late files; a GOT IT or a day-before YES that is from another consultant, or has no name beside it (BW, BX), with the cells to clear (the arrival time in CH among them); OVER THE DAILY CAP, when a consultant holds more hearings on one date than the Bench tab allows; THE OFFICE HAS X, NOT Y (send the replacement notice); our date-change request still open (BI, BJ); a homeowner's notice with the wrong name or date (BK, BL); and who to tell about a change (BN, BO), which stays on every row, also after the hearing and at NOT HELD, until the OK is linked. It also prints the office's own route while the office has not confirmed the consultant's name in writing (Offices F; when the office has changed how it works, the block until a person approves the change, and after that the new route from Offices M, so nobody emails an office that asked for a call), the office's replacement route (Offices G), NO HOMEOWNER NOTICE ON RECORD for a coming hearing with a yes and nothing in BK or BL, the next step after a missed hearing, and the proofs still missing after a hearing that was held. It prints VIDEO ROOM ONLY, NO LINK where column AV holds a room letter and the office has not said that is all it sends; the question to send where a clerk's or a consultant's receipt names no version (AZ or AY empty while AX is filled); FIRST CASE AT OPENING; and a consultant's own arrival time (CH) that is later than the firm needs. A send-by moment (BM, BB) or an office deadline (AW) with a time of day reads as past once that hour has gone by on the clock in Settings B15. Each line says what to do.

Changes from an office after a consultant said yes (room, link, time) go into column AV the same day and to the consultant as a change notice ("Reply OK"), unless the consultant's own message shows they already have it; the day-before text prints column AV. A date moves only when the county says so in writing: a phone report is noted, the consultant is warned the same day, and the row keeps the old date until the notice arrives. A moved hearing needs a new yes (clear G2). Anyone who declines a slot goes into column BC, so they are not asked again for that docket. Who signs anything owed is in column BP, from the office's rule: Offices AC holds one of three answers chosen from a list (the consultant who attends, the representative on the office's record, the homeowner) or the question still to ask, and Offices AG holds the answer for a withdrawal statement where that differs. BP adds the form of signature the office accepts (Offices AD) once it is known.
Calendar: built from the sheet, never the other way round

The Calendar tab lists every hearing with a yes that counts (a hearing by written statement is left out: nobody attends it), in the columns a calendar import reads (Google Calendar's CSV format). Every day after the 2:00 p.m. review, and the same day a date, time, room or consultant changes, the coordinator downloads the tab as CSV (File, Download, CSV) and replaces the events in the firm's hearing calendar, which consultants may view but not edit. An event ends after the office's own hearing length (Offices AP), or else the minutes in Settings B11, and a video or telephone hearing is placed at the office only where the office says its video room is there (Offices AL). Column J of the tab gives each event's office hours from UTC: when offices are in more than one time zone, filter on it and download one file for each zone, because the times in the file are the office's local time. Rows below the last event are empty. An edit in a calendar moves nothing: only the county moves a hearing, in writing (Velloran, messages 9 to 11; Orimere, messages 17 and 18). The Record check tab catches any case record that followed a calendar edit. The "Calendar file" tab prints the same events as an iCalendar file with the times in UTC (see the last rows of this tab); it is the first way to fill a calendar, and the CSV is the second.

Bench lists every consultant with their preferred channel, the counties they may work in, the most hearings they take in a day, the weekdays they promised, their preferences and the season letter, and their mobile number for texts with the link to their agreement to be texted (columns O and P: questions for the season letter until answered; column Q flags every consultant with no number or no agreement to be texted and says which steps cannot reach them, and a consultant whose two stated channels differ). Availability holds anything a consultant says about being free or not free, with the link. Offices holds each county's routes from the packet, what its own messages added, its notice form, who signs, its time zone, and the questions still to ask (amber); when an office says something new about how it works, write it in column M the same day with its date in column AT: no notice goes to that office until a person approves the change in columns AQ and AR, with a date on or after the date in AT. Holidays holds each county's closures; every working-day count uses the hearing's own county. An office's own rules are numbers and lists that the formulas read: its standing naming deadline in working days (Offices AF), who signs (AC, AG), its own travel gaps (AI, AJ; empty means the Settings value, and the travel check uses the larger of the two offices' values) and the fields its notice or form must carry (AK), which the "Notices on file" tab checks field by field. The Offices tab also holds what a video room means at the office (AL, chosen from a list), its opening hours as times (AM, AN), whom to reach before opening on a hearing morning (AO) and the length of one hearing (AP; a question or an empty cell means Settings B11). The formulas read 40 consultants (Bench rows 2 to 41) and 39 offices (Offices rows 2 to 40); cell A1 of the Dockets tab and the Measures tab say in red when a name is typed below those rows or two offices share a name. Name an office "County, ST" when two states have a county of the same name. A partial decline ("I can take the 9:30 but not the 9:00") is one Availability row marked not free, with the start and the end of the declined hearing in From and To.

Paste the case system's export into the Record check tab: every record that disagrees with the sheet on date, time, consultant, case files or status is flagged, and is corrected in the case system the same day. A record that says "canceled" is flagged until the office's written confirmation is linked in column AF of the Hearings tab, whatever "Hearing still on?" says; until then "scheduled" is the right record. Someone who does not keep the sheet opens every proof link of the 10 hearings on the "Friday sample" tab, writes down how many did not prove their cell, and copies the week's measures into the weekly log on the Measures tab. Ask each office about every DECISION DUE row. That log is the baseline: every target is reset from it at the live-week-4 review.

On the Settings tab replace the example date in B2 with =TODAY() and the example time of day in B15 with =MOD(NOW(),1), keep B6 at full, and name the evening reader in B9. Fill the Offices, Bench and Holidays tabs once a season, and ask the amber questions in desk week 2. The Day 1 count and Hours tabs give the numbers the software decision needs. A spreadsheet cannot lock a formula, so the Measures tab counts Status cells that were typed over; it must read 0.
Added on 20 Nov 2026 (the rules of Part I of the rule book)

An office that changes how it works. Write what it said in column M of the Offices tab and the date in column AT. From that moment column BE of each of its hearings that still needs a notice, column N of the Dockets tab and column N of the Offices tab read NO NOTICE GOES TO THIS OFFICE UNTIL A PERSON APPROVES THE CHANGE TODAY, print no route, and the hearing goes to the TOP OF LIST with the words NOTICE BLOCKED. A person reads the change and approves it by typing their name in column AQ and the date in column AR, and types in column AS whether the office still accepts the old route (yes, no or not known). From then on the new route in column M is printed as the route. The old route in column F is printed as a second route only while AS says yes or not known; when AS says no it is printed nowhere. When the office confirms the change in writing, type the date in column L, then move M into F and G and clear M, AQ, AR, AS and AT. If that is forgotten nothing goes wrong: once L holds a date on or after the date in AT, the sheet treats M as the route. When the new route needs a call (the word "call" in column M), column BE prints the call with the office's hours (Offices D): type the call in Y (what), Z (who) and AA (by when). A call never closes a check.

An office that cannot find our notice. Paste the link to its message or call note in column CP of the hearing, and in column CQ the date our notice went (or the link to the sent message). While the office has not confirmed the name in writing, column BE reads that THE NOTICE WAS SENT but THE OFFICE CANNOT FIND IT, with the step (resend the completed form or notice by the approved route and call in the office's hours), and the daily list reads TOP OF LIST with the words OFFICE CANNOT FIND OUR NOTICE, so the row is not read as "nothing sent".

A consultant who reports ill. Add the "not free" row on the Availability tab as before, choose "illness" in its column I and type the day they said it in column J. Every hearing that consultant holds from that day to 7 calendar days after it (Settings B18, our suggestion) goes to the TOP OF LIST with the words ILLNESS REPORTED, and column BE reads that they REPORTED ILL: ASK TODAY WHETHER THEY WILL ATTEND, AND LINE UP A BACKUP before the office's naming deadline. The line clears when their own yes is linked in column CT of the hearing with its date in column CU, on or after the day of the report.

A consultant with no mobile number. Column R of the Bench tab reads 0 (no number in column O), 1 (a number, but no link to their agreement to be texted in column P) or 2. "Ask next" on the Dockets tab writes (EMAIL ONLY) or (CALL OR EMAIL, NO TEXT) after such a name, and from 3 working days before a hearing column BE says that the day-before message goes by email and which calls cannot be made. The Measures tab counts the consultants with no number.

Before the firm asks an office to move a hearing. Column CS of the hearing takes the link to the dated note of who on the bench was asked first and said no, and column CR the link to the homeowner's yes to the new date; they belong with BI and BJ. While a request is out (BI typed, no answer linked in BJ) and either link is missing, column BE says so. A settlement: column BE lists what is still missing, namely the homeowner's written acceptance (BG), the office's receipt of the signed settlement (O), the office's written word that the hearing is off its schedule (AF, the same cell as for a cancellation or a withdrawal) and the date by which it must reach the office (BA). Until AF is linked the hearing stays staffed and on its docket. When an office asks for something owed, column BE first asks to check whether the current case files already hold it: the sheet cannot read a file, so it prints the check on every such row.

Time zones and the calendar file. Column AU of the Offices tab says whether the office changes its clocks (yes, no, or the question). When it says yes the sheet adds one hour to the office's standard hours from UTC (column W) for a hearing dated from the second Sunday of March up to the day before the first Sunday of November (the United States rule); otherwise W is used as typed. Column CV of the Hearings tab holds the result for each hearing, and every text and the Calendar tab use it. The "Calendar file" tab prints the same events as an iCalendar file with the times in UTC: select column A from cell A1 down to the line END:VCALENDAR, copy it, paste it into a plain text file, save it as hearings.ics and import that file. UTC times show at the right hour in every calendar, whatever time zone the calendar is set to. The CSV download of the Calendar tab stays as the second way; its times are the office's local time, so each calendar must be set to the office's time zone before the import.
Added on 21 Nov 2026 (the rules of Part J of the rule book)

A consultant who is not free at the arrival time. When a "not free" row of the Availability tab covers the time the firm needs a consultant at the office (their first case less the minutes in Settings B16, Hearings CL), column BE of each hearing they hold on that docket reads ARRIVAL NOT SETTLED, names what they said and the two steps (ask the time they can arrive and type it in column CH, or ask the office to hear the case later), and the daily list carries the words ARRIVAL NOT SETTLED. Until CH holds a time the day-before text says that the arrival time is being settled and prints no time; once CH holds a time the text prints that time. A time in CH that is later than the consultant's first case settles nothing: the words ARRIVAL NOT SETTLED stay, column BE says so, and the text prints no time. Type the time in CH on every hearing the consultant holds on the docket.

A clearer copy already asked for. Type the date of the request in column DA of the hearing (or paste the link to the request when its date is not known) and ask nothing more. While the office has not receipted the document (no link in column O), column BE reads that the copy was asked for on that date, DO NOT ASK AGAIN, and when the fallback falls due: noon on the working day that Settings B14 names (1 = the next working day, by the office's own holidays). From that moment the daily list carries the words FALLBACK DUE and column BE orders the fallback: the signing link to the person who signs (column BP), then a call. Nothing is signed for a settlement or a withdrawal until the homeowner's written yes is linked in column BG: while it is missing, the line at the due time orders the call to the homeowner instead, and the signing link goes as soon as BG is linked. Clear DA when a readable copy has come.

A first case at opening. On the days column BE prints FIRST CASE AT OPENING (from two working days before the hearing), the daily list carries the words OPENING NOT ARRANGED, also when every proof is linked. When the end-of-docket request and the alternate are arranged, paste the link to the office's message or to the dated note in column DB: the line and the words stop.

A hearing the firm asked an office to move. When the office answers, link its answer in BJ and choose "moved" or "refused" in column DI. A hearing that was moved at our request keeps two lines in column BE until they are settled: the homeowner's yes to the new date is not on record (a person calls the homeowner today and links the yes in CR), and no record that the bench was asked first (CS). Column DH takes the name of a consultant who had already accepted the hearing when the request was made, with the link to their yes: column BE then says that the request was made for a hearing a consultant had already accepted, and it says the same while a request is out for a hearing that a consultant holds. Column AY of the Offices tab holds the office's last day for a change request as a number of working days before the hearing (question 14 of the season email to offices, number 38 in the kit's list): from 3 working days before that day (Settings B4), and after it, column BE says so on a hearing with a request out or with no consultant.

A settlement. Column DC takes the link to the settlement offer on file and column DD the date by which the offer must be accepted. The list SETTLEMENT, STILL MISSING in column BE now starts with the offer and its acceptance date, and prints THE OFFER MUST BE ACCEPTED BY with the date. The sheet treats a row as a settlement when column N holds the letters "settle" (settlement, settled), or when DC holds a link or DD a date; with DC or DD filled and no such word in N, column BE asks for the word in N, because only N makes the row count as owed.

The homeowner and the office on the telephone. Columns DE and DF hold the homeowner's name and customer number, column DG their contact (a question until the firm fills it from the client file). Where a line orders a call to the homeowner, column BE adds THE HOMEOWNER TO CALL with the name, the number and the contact, and ONE CALL COVERS with the other hearing of the same customer number that also needs a call (or how many there are), and the daily list of a hearing still to come carries the words CALL THE HOMEOWNER. Column AZ of the Offices tab holds the office's daytime telephone number and the clerk to ask for (question 15 of the season email to offices, number 40 in the kit's list): where a line orders a call to the office, column BE adds TO CALL THE OFFICE with that number, or NUMBER NOT ON RECORD and the cell.

Whose clock. The line TELL in column BE and the notice "Tell the office" on the Dockets tab now carry the sentence that the times are the office's time, with its hours from UTC, as the offers and the day-before texts already do. On the Reader suggestions tab a proposal from a message that repeats an earlier message for the same cell reads REPEAT: THE CELL KEEPS ITS FIRST LINK: nothing is typed for it. Offices columns N ("Ask again?") and Z (signed bench names) hold their formulas on every row from 2 to 40, so an eleventh office typed on row 12 is flagged like the first ten.

A consultant's question. When a consultant asks something about a hearing they hold or were offered (which date, what has changed, whether to prepare), type who asked, the answer and the message in column BN of each hearing it concerns, as for a wrong belief, and send the answer the same day. Column BE prints TELL with those words until column BO holds the link to their OK or to their own later message, so a question cannot stay unanswered unseen. In the example: AX-103 and AX-104 (message 12), AX-115 (message 48), AX-111 and AX-112 (message 35), AX-117 and AX-118 (message 54). The foot of the Reader suggestions tab lists the questions the tools found in the example messages, and the repeats: a message that says again what the linked message already says changes no cell.
Added later on 21 Nov 2026 (the rules of Part K of the rule book)

A hearing that an office moves. Type the new date in column D and the date the hearing had before in column DR, clear the consultant and the yes (H and J), and move the link in K into a note in column Y: the office recorded our representative for the old date. The sheet guards this. On a hearing marked as moved (DR holds another date than D, or DI says moved) the link in K counts only when column DQ holds the date in D, and with a date in DQ it counts on any hearing only while that date is the date in D. Until then the check G3 is open and column BE prints the written question to the office: IS (the name) STILL ON YOUR RECORD FOR (the new date). When the office answers, link its answer in K and type the new date in DQ. The limit: a hearing whose date is typed over in column D with nothing in DR, DI or DQ is not seen as moved. Type the dates in DQ, DR, DW and DX as dates: a date typed there as text reads as no date, so a move typed as text in DR is not seen either, and cell A1 of the Dockets tab names the row and the column until the cell holds a date. In the example: AX-105 (messages 16 and 17).

The homeowner after a move. While DR holds the old date of a hearing still to come and column DS holds no link, the daily list carries CALL THE HOMEOWNER and column BE orders the call and the corrected homeowner notice, with the homeowner's name and contact. Link the dated call note, the homeowner's own message or the notice sent in DS. A hearing moved at our own request (DI says moved) keeps the lines of the rule above it instead: the homeowner's yes goes in CR. In the example: AX-115 (message 47).

Where a result comes from. Type who reported the result and when in column DT and link the note or the message in DU; a result with no source prints a line in column BE. A result that fits no value of the list (for example "they are giving us more time") is typed as "reported: not clear": the status reads RESULT NOT CLEAR, the row stays on the daily list, and column BE orders the question to the consultant and to the office the same day. Choose the real result when one of them answers. In the example: AX-119 and AX-120 (messages 57 and 59).

Who decided a date-change request. Type the name of the person who decided to ask an office to move a hearing, and the date, in column DV. While a request is out or was made and DV is empty, column BE says that no named person decided it. A request the office refused that was made without the bench being asked first (CS) or without the homeowner's yes (CR) keeps one line in column BE, as a record; it puts nothing on the daily list.

Where a hearing in person is held. Column BA of the Offices tab holds the office's street address, the hearing room and where to report. The day-before text and the calendar entry print it, and column BE prints it for whoever takes a hearing over (a consultant who is not free, an illness report, a name the office does not have). While BA is empty or a question they read ADDRESS NOT ON RECORD with the cell, and from 3 working days before the hearing column BE orders the question to the office.

Dates, not words. Column AA (by when) takes a date. When a message says today, tomorrow or this week, type the day the message arrived in column DX and the real date in AA; words in AA print a line in column BE. Column DW takes the day an office's notice arrived: type it for every paper notice (column BE asks for it at an office whose column BB on the Offices tab says yes) and wherever a deadline counts from the arrival. In the example DX and AA of AX-107 and AX-108 are the example's own reading of message 24, as their notes say, because no message carries a date.
Added on 21 Nov 2026, round 19 (the rules of Part L of the rule book)

Who asked for a date change. Every office lets the firm, consultants and homeowners ask it to change a hearing date (Offices I). Column EB records who asked: type the firm, the homeowner, or the consultant and their name, with the message number. When EB names a consultant, column BE tells the coordinator to ask that consultant the same day why, and to tell them the rule: date requests go through the firm, which asks the homeowner and the bench first. If the office moves the hearing, it is handled as any office move (the old date in DR, the office's record for the new date in K and DQ, the homeowner's new date in DS). While DR holds an earlier date of a hearing still to come, the move was not made at our request (DI) and EB is empty, column BE asks who asked. In the example: the firm for AX-103 and AX-104 (message 8) and for AX-105 and AX-106 (message 15), the homeowner for AX-115 (message 47).

Who may appear and sign in each state. Column S of the Bench tab holds the states in which a consultant may appear and sign for a homeowner, from counsel's answer (Offices R) and the consultant's own licence or registration. It is a question for all six consultants. Once it holds an answer, the "Who can take it" tab and Ask next leave the consultant out of every docket of an office in another state (Offices B), and column BE of a hearing whose consultant may not appear or sign there says so and orders the step. While it is a question, Ask next marks each consultant it concerns (STATES: ASK) and ends with a short warning: the offer may go, and counsel's answer is chased. Where something owed is still to be signed, column BE asks the question before anything more is signed: at Brindlefen (AX-109 and AX-110) the office returned a withdrawal statement that named Owen Tarris, because Priya Marden is the representative on its record (message 28).

Case files after a consultant leaves a hearing. Column EC takes the date on which the earlier consultant's access to the case files was removed (the folder links sent, or their written word that they deleted the files), or the words files were never sent. While EC is empty, column BE prints a line when the GOT IT in M is from someone who is no longer the consultant on the row (BW), when the hearing is off and its consultant had the files, or when column BC names someone who declined the hearing or was taken off it. In the example EC is empty on every row, because no message shows that access was removed: Maya Venn on AX-101, AX-113 and AX-114 (messages 38, 41 and 42), Leo Arlen on AX-103, AX-104 and AX-115, Nora Pell on AX-106. The lines of round 19 put nothing on the daily list.

headers.F: Open hearings (numbers with no consultant's yes)
headers.H: The offer, one text for the open hearings of the docket
headers.I: The day-before text, one for each consultant on the docket
headers.J: Row on the Hearings tab: last hearing (formula)
headers.L: Row on the Hearings tab: first hearing (formula)
headers.N: Tell the office: who attends, from yes replies only, and the office's own route
headers.O: Ask next, in this order (Bench and Availability tabs; anyone who declined, said they are not free, is full or cannot travel in time is left out; (EMAIL ONLY) after a name means no mobile number is on file, so no text and no call can reach them; (CALL OR EMAIL, NO TEXT) means a number is on file without their agreement to be texted)
headers.P: Video or telephone hearings on the docket with no link or number yet: Hearings CJ is 4 or 5 (formula)

cells.A: One row for each office, day and format from today on: that is a docket. The rows are formulas over the Hearings tab, so keep that tab sorted by date, then office, then time. Hearings that are marked as not on, that have no date, or that are over, are not in a docket. Every Monday, offer each docket of the next three weeks whole to one consultant, unless the column "Offer this docket to" names someone who is already on it. Video dockets of different counties on one day can go to the same person if the times do not overlap. Sent as scheduled messages from the shared mailbox or the text line, these texts replace one offer and one confirmation per hearing. The offer lists only the hearings that are still open, each with its number in the docket. When an offer goes, type the consultant's name in column BY of the Hearings tab on each hearing offered, and clear it at their no: an offer that is out counts toward that consultant's daily cap. The day-before text is written once for each consultant who holds a hearing on the docket, with that consultant's own first time and number of hearings. Where a docket has several consultants, each text begins with "To" and the name. They go to the firm's own consultants only, never to a county or a homeowner.

cells.B: Larkmere

cells.A: Whenever a consultant says when they are free or not free ("I have left the morning free", "I cannot attend on June 13", "I am ill"), the person who reads it adds a row here the same day, with the link. Free: "Ask next" on the Dockets tab puts them near the top for that day. Not free: they are left out of "Ask next" for that time, and any hearing they hold then turns its G2 check open, with a red line in column BE of the Hearings tab: offer it down "Ask next" now. Empty From and To mean the whole day. For a partial decline ("I can take the 9:30 but not the 9:00") type the start and the end of the declined hearing in From and To (9:00 and 9:30): a period that ends exactly when another hearing starts does not touch that hearing, and the same time typed twice covers nothing. A dropout is handled by this one row, whatever the hour. When they say they are ill, choose "illness" in column I and type the day they said it in column J: every hearing they hold from that day to the number of days in Settings B18 after it then asks, in column BE of the Hearings tab, whether they will attend.

cells.A: Codes, best first: 1 already at this office that day; 2 said they are free then (Availability tab); 3 primary or second consultant for this office (Offices X and Y), or promised this weekday (Bench I); 4 their standing preference fits the time and format (Bench K and L); 5 on the bench and allowed in this county; 6 working elsewhere that day, with the travel gap met (Settings B11 to B13, or the larger gap either office asks for in Offices AI and AJ; each hearing lasts its own office's length, Offices AP, or else Settings B11; a video hearing in a room at the office, Offices AL, counts as in person). x: declined this docket, said they are not free then, already full that day, or working elsewhere too close in time. A consultant's day counts the hearings they hold and the hearings on offer to them (Hearings BY) on every docket of that date. Empty: not allowed in this county, or column T of the Bench tab holds counsel's answer and it does not name the state of this office (Offices B; round 19). The Dockets tab reads column AV. Column BE holds the state of the docket's office. Row 2 marks a consultant (STATES: ASK) while their Bench S is a question or empty: Ask next then ends with a short warning.

cells.A: A clearer copy already asked for: working days to wait before the signing link
cells.C: The copy asked for gets until noon on the next working day; only then does the signing link go, so the consultant never gets two requests at once. Column DM of the Hearings tab reads this number: the fallback falls due at noon on the working day this many working days after the date in Hearings DA, by the office's own holidays, and column BE prints that moment. On a settlement or a withdrawal the signing link goes only once the homeowner's written yes is linked in BG: until then the due fallback is a call to the homeowner
cells.J: TYPE WHO REPORTED IT AND WHEN IN DT

cells.C: Example: 2:00 p.m., the hour of the daily review. When live, replace with =MOD(NOW(),1). Column BE of the Hearings tab reads a case-file send-by (BM), an owed send-by (BB) or an office deadline (AW) as past once that moment is before today (B2) plus this time. A deadline typed as a date with no time is past only from the next day. If this cell is empty, only the date counts
cells.J: LINK THE NOTE OR MESSAGE IN DU

cells.A: Arrival: minutes before their first case that the firm needs a consultant at the office
cells.C: The plan's own rule, not a figure from the packet. The day-before text for an in-person hearing gives it as a clock time ("be at the office by 10:30 a.m."), and the coordinator phones when no ARRIVED has come by then. Where the office asks for more minutes on a hearing (Hearings CI), the larger number is used; where it asks for less (Fenwick Vale: 15, message 40), this one stands, so the text names one time only. A consultant who names a later time (Hearings CH) gets a reply the same day: column BE says so
cells.J: NO NAMED PERSON DECIDED THIS DATE-CHANGE REQUEST: TYPE WHO DECIDED IT AND WHEN IN DV.

cells.A: A hearing starts "at opening" when it starts less than this many minutes after its office opens
cells.C: The office opens at the time in column AM of the Offices tab (9:00 a.m. at all ten example offices). The firm's call to the office, 15 minutes before a hearing, cannot be made for such a hearing. From two working days before, column BE of the Hearings tab prints FIRST CASE AT OPENING, and the end-of-docket request and the alternate are arranged while the office is open
cells.J: ON RECORD: THE REQUEST THE OFFICE REFUSED WAS MADE

cells.A: Illness: calendar days after a report in which the consultant's hearings are checked
cells.C: Our suggestion, not a figure from the packet. When a "not free" row on the Availability tab has the reason "illness", every hearing that consultant holds from the day of the report (Availability J, or else A) to this many calendar days after it prints REPORTED ILL in column BE of the Hearings tab and goes to the TOP OF LIST, until their own yes after the report is linked in Hearings CT with its date in CU
cells.J: WITHOUT THE BENCH BEING ASKED FIRST (CS)

cells.A: Illness reports on the Availability tab (formula)

cells.C: Round 17. While it is 0 the Hearings tab does not look for a consultant who is not free at their arrival time (column DK), which keeps the sheet fast: a "not free" row for the whole day already takes the consultant off the hearing
